x: The most prominent of these is Derek Howie. Having competed in three Nationals this year any doubts as to his authenticity to compete have been completely dispelled.
We must not overlook the great performance of our new member Derek Howie. Making his first appearance in a National Championship he competed as an individual and finished in 14th place in 71m.53s.
The only one who did walk to form was non-scoring Derek Howie who in spite of his efforts has been overlooked by the Scottish selectors for Edmonton.
He was closely followed by Derek Howie, walking as an individual, with John Hall taking 3rd place in the Club Championship. Carl Lawton and Bob Picton completed the team.

Congratulations on some great walking Graham, its good to see you back in such great form - a great day. Allan Callow and Derek Howie (who had competed in the longer race the previous day) were our other representatives.

Others worthy of mention are Paul Blagg, Junior International; Richard Dorman, 2nd in the National Junior; Mike Nicholls, 3rd in the National Youths; Graham Seatter and Allan Callow, Commonwealth Games competitors; Derek Howie, Scottish International; Linda Nicholls, 2nd in the W.A.A.A.

Brighton, on August 19th, saw a Belgrave 1, 2, 3 in another 20kms event with Carl winning in 98:28 from John Hall and Derek Howie. Glutton for punishment that he is, Carl was out the following day for the South Western Counties open track 10kms at Weymouth.

Our other starter, Derek Howie, entered as an individual, put up a plucky performance for his first "Brighton". For well over half way he was always near the leaders but over the last miles he began to lose places and became unsteady so wisely retired with just nine miles left.
It was good to see Derek Howie on one of his trips from Stirling. Unfortunately he developed some leg trouble which proved a drawback - he is having this put right before competing again.

Derek Howie, now a B.A. recently spent two weeks in Farnham Park Hospital, Slough having a back ailment sorted out, he went there thinking that it was a holiday camp and did not realise that he was expected to do exercises all the time.
Gerry Cameron was the Team Manager for the Scottish walking team last year, in a match against Wales in which Derek Howie was competing.
D. Howie finished 5th in the Scottish 20Kms on 18th May.
